description: Evidence-led staged evaluation and implementation of Laya Multilingual. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-laya-decision-service.md. Preserve current authority, dirty work, and independent hardware acceleration plan.

acceptance_criteria: Reuses an existing task/API surface and canonical authorization/identity.
Typed category options are server-owned; no arbitrary prompt/transcript/source input.
Response includes success, decision ID, mode/status, category, suggestion/reason codes, evidence IDs, uncertainty, and only verified runtime metadata.
No tool execution, permission/task-state changes, receipt creation, or deterministic override.
task_laya_advisory.blocker: No candidate category has passed independent Hub evaluation.
task_laya_advisory.description: Stage dependency: expose explicit typed advisory through an existing API/tool only after the category passes evaluation. Caller cannot set mode, identity, permissions, or global automation. Result is a proposal; errors/abstention remain explicit.
task_laya_advisory.next_action: Keep unregistered until a category passes the evaluation gate.
task_laya_advisory.title: Expose explicit typed advisory call after validation

acceptance_criteria: Non-private fixtures have independent labels and group-safe splits.
Compare current deterministic baseline and Laya on identical cases.
Report quality and abstention by category and language.
Count schema/protocol tokens, tool roundtrips, local compute, and latency separately.
No quality claim without sufficient held-out cases.
task_laya_evaluation.blocker: No approved category/minimal input/privacy scope, independent production labels, paired deterministic baseline, fixed thresholds, or sealed group-safe holdout. Exact compatibility between the pinned checkpoint and current training package is untested. Device-specific ONNX/provider support is unproven; no runtime adapter is connected.
task_laya_evaluation.description: Current official upstream docs now provide `laya-train` and `laya.train.finetune` for a local checkpoint directory, on CUDA/MPS/CPU. Accepted JSONL shapes are `{state, questions, expected}` or `{state, questions, gold}`; the existing train export matches the hard-label shape, but merged output lacks global group/label provenance and remains training-only. The pinned multilingual model is 322M mmBERT-base; its model card reports weak typed-decision zero-shot results and uncalibrated/overconfident probabilities, so specialize one copy for a single approved workflow and calibrate against held-out labels. Provider lists and upstream ONNX export do not prove this graph runs on each vendor device; upstream ONNXAgent is documented for CPU. No package/checkpoint compatibility, Hub data fit, hardware provider, or runtime measurements are verified.
task_laya_evaluation.next_action: Keep production capture, inference, training, shadow, and advisory stopped. After category/input/privacy, labels, baseline, thresholds, and provider authorization are established, validate the pinned checkpoint/package pair and candidate JSONL with the documented dry-run, fine-tune one multilingual copy for that workflow, then compare against the paired baseline on a sealed holdout and measure tokens, latency, quality, and actual provider/device separately.
task_laya_evaluation.title: Build paired fixtures and evaluate quality, cost, and latency

acceptance_criteria: Current plan and repository state reviewed; no duplicate plan.
Laya model suitability and concrete decision tasks evidenced or precise blockers documented.
Implement safe bounded infrastructure or integration without automatic authority or side effects.
Make session lifecycle state observable without asserting hardware release.
Batch training-candidate intake is scoped, per-example consented, atomic, bounded, and deduplicated.
Targeted verification recorded; remaining stages and blockers documented.
task_laya_evidence.description: Safe Laya groundwork is implemented: strict typed decision contracts, metadata-only telemetry, one shared 600-second idle lifecycle polled by the existing scheduler, consented candidate storage in the existing Agent State database, deterministic group-safe snapshots and train-only export, diagnostics redaction/export, normal status and ZIP lifecycle metadata, bounded capture_batch, and encrypted train-only ZIP pooling. Dashboard-enabled diagnostics consent export now passes after fixing the test's forwarded-scope expectation and close race; request-body HTTP 408 preservation has an isolated regression. Focused current suite: 126 passed. No connected provider/inference adapter; no inference, training, extra install/download, hardware release claim, or measured token/quality/latency gain.
task_laya_evidence.next_action: Evidence and safe infrastructure stage complete. Keep production capture, shadow, and advisory disabled pending approved category/input/privacy scope, independent labels, paired deterministic baseline, fixed thresholds, and qualified provider.
task_laya_evidence.title: Inspect Hub decision surfaces and verify model provenance

acceptance_criteria: Reuse existing telemetry, report, and ZIP paths; no second store or exporter.
Report shadow separately from explicit advisory with coverage, status, latency, backend, abstention, errors, fallback, and skips.
Expose shared lifecycle status through existing Hub status and laya/report.json.runtime without claiming hardware placement or release.
Normal ZIP contains metadata only, schema/time/manifest, provenance, evaluation summaries, and included/skipped/missing counts.
Training candidate text is excluded unless separately opted in through an authorized existing export route.
Merge multiple existing encrypted ZIP train members without extracting unrelated files or persisting passwords.
Validate rows against the upstream training JSONL shape; deduplicate exact rows and reject conflicting labels for identical state/questions.
Write merged output atomically with provenance counts only; mark train-only and evaluation_eligible=false because source exports omit global group identities.
task_laya_export.blocker: No connected runtime adapter/provider or evaluated decision category. Runtime backend/latency provenance cannot be reported; merged training rows omit global task/session/group provenance and cannot form pooled evaluation data. Independent labels, paired deterministic baseline, fixed thresholds, and approved input/privacy scope are absent.
task_laya_export.description: Existing encrypted diagnostics ZIP retains metadata-only Laya report and lifecycle data; candidate tables, assignments and linked capture traces are removed from disposable snapshots. Candidate JSONL requires explicit consent, authorized repository scope, a valid snapshot, and verified train rows. `laya-dataset-merge` reads only encrypted train members, validates shape/size, deduplicates exact rows, rejects conflicting labels, writes atomically, and marks output training-only/evaluation-ineligible because group provenance is absent. Telemetry now summarizes shadow and advisory separately with category/status/reason counts plus abstentions, errors, and skips. Coverage, latency, backend, and fallback metrics are explicitly unavailable because denominator/runtime provenance is not recorded. Focused checks: 47 tests passed across Laya telemetry, decision contracts, and diagnostics export. No runtime provider is connected; actual backend/latency and paired evaluation remain unavailable.
task_laya_export.next_action: Keep candidate pooling training-only and production capture stopped. Once approved category/input/privacy scope, independent labels, paired baseline, fixed thresholds, and a qualified provider are available, add authentic runtime denominator/backend/latency/fallback evidence and complete the paired evaluation. Preserve explicit unavailable states until then.
task_laya_export.title: Extend existing reports and authorized ZIP

acceptance_criteria: Closed categories and category-specific option enums
Server-bound mode and canonical identity on mapping and direct construction
Only whitelisted choices; no completion attestation, actual watchdog command, or skipped validation
Metadata projection excludes raw payload
Targeted tests and compile pass
task_laya_foundation.description: Strict side-effect-free request/result contract. Request mapping rejects mode/identity spoofing; direct construction enforces same server-bound identity and category option allowlists. No `abstain`, `verified`, executable watchdog commands or repeated-work skips appear as suggestions. Hub route suggestions use existing ModelExecutionPolicy tiers; watchdog values use recommendation labels. Result reason codes are finite and required for non-success. No model or Hub route registration; 22 targeted tests pass, compileall passes.
task_laya_foundation.next_action: Keep unregistered until independent category labels, deterministic baseline and runtime gates pass.
task_laya_foundation.title: Implement only independently useful contract infrastructure

acceptance_criteria: Shadow off leaves the current path unchanged.
Inference failures, timeout, overload, and invalid output cannot block or alter Hub behavior.
Telemetry stores only allowlisted metadata and excludes raw text/model output.
One category passes a predeclared held-out quality and utility gate.
task_laya_shadow.blocker: Blocked by missing independent labels, baseline, and evaluated export path.
task_laya_shadow.description: Stage dependency: requires evaluation and metadata-only report/export support. Add one disabled-by-default, nonblocking category only after independent labels, paired baseline, and fixed thresholds pass.
task_laya_shadow.next_action: Do not invoke Laya before prerequisites pass.
task_laya_shadow.title: Add one evaluated metadata-only shadow category

title: Laya decision service: safe staged integration
